notes: bf16 column holds FP16 (Pascal has no BF16 and no Tensor Cores; non-tensor FP16 rate). NVLink 1: 4 links x 40 GB/s bidirectional. First shipped in DGX-1 (mid-2016).

fp64 = FP64 Tensor Core (34 TFLOPS non-tensor). Datasheet quotes TF32 989 / BF16 1979 / FP8 3958 / INT8 3958 with sparsity; halved here. 700 W is the configurable maximum.

Two reticle-limited dies joined by 10 TB/s NV-HBI. die_area is an Est.: NVIDIA does not publish die area; ~800 mm2 assumed (~93% of the 858 mm2 reticle, like GH100's 814 mm2). 192 GB physical, 180 GB usable in HGX; some datasheets list 7.7 TB/s. HGX sparse figures (FP4 18, FP8 9 PFLOPS) halved. PCIe generation left blank (not verified this session).

TDP 1,200 W per GPU is widely reported (GB200 superchip ~2,700 W incl. Grace), not an NVIDIA per-GPU spec. die_area Est. as for B200. Volume shipments ramped Q1 2025.

FP64 cut to ~1.25 TFLOPS and INT8 sharply reduced (left blank: conflicting board figures). 12-high HBM3E (8 x 36 GB); some datasheets list 270 GB usable at 7.7 TB/s. 1,100 W configurable (not an NVIDIA per-GPU spec for all SKUs). ConnectX-8 with integrated PCIe Gen6 switch.

Per-GPU values = GB300 NVL72 rack / 72: FP4 1,080 PFLOPS dense; FP8 720 PFLOPS and INT8 24 POPS are sparse (halved); FP64 100 TFLOPS rack. 20 TB rack HBM3E (288 GB per GPU nominal). As announced at CES 2026 (2026-01-05) and GTC 2026. NVFP4: 50 PFLOPS inference (uses Transformer Engine adaptive compression) vs 35 PFLOPS training; 35 used as dense. HBM4 bandwidth revised ~Sep-2026 from 22 to 19.2 TB/s and NVLink 6 from 3.6 to 3.0 TB/s per GPU (NVIDIA: reflects volume-production specs; HGX page still shows old figures). FP64 33 TFLOPS native (200 TFLOPS DGEMM via emulation). TDP reported 1,800 W Max-Q / 2,300 W Max-P (SemiAnalysis/Kuo), not NVIDIA-published. die_area Est. (two reticle-sized compute dies). Name first shown Computex 2024; volume ramp H2 2026.
